subject: AtlasPay tokenization disruption — closure plan, owners & QBR sync
messages:
From: Kevin Lowe <kevin.lowe@atlaspay.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, integration@atlaspay.com
Date: Tue, 29 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent tokenization failures impacting AtlasPay checkout

Hi Ben / Marissa,

We saw intermittent tokenization failures impacting ~5-7% of checkouts across US-West region between 07:45 and 08:20 PDT this morning. Symptoms: 502s from the tokenization endpoint and duplicate authorizations for a small subset of customers. We opened a support ticket but wanted to escalate to your team because this has direct SLA implications for AtlasPay (we have a financial reconciliation window today).

What we need:
- Confirmation of root cause and ETA for fixes
- Whether this qualifies for an SLA credit and, if so, the expected process/timeline
- Any temporary mitigations we should apply on our side to avoid duplicate authorizations

I've attached our sample request/response pairs and a short log snip. Please let us know ASAP — the reconciliation starts 11:00 PDT.

Thanks,
Kevin Lowe
Director, Integrations — AtlasPay
kevin.lowe@atlaspay.com

Attachments: atlaspay_snippets.log (6 KB)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Kevin Lowe <kevin.lowe@atlaspay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Mar 2028 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent tokenization failures impacting AtlasPay checkout

Kevin — thanks for the heads up and the log samples. I'm assigning priority to this now. Quick status:

- We saw a transient regression in the tokenization cache invalidation code during a rolling kernel update in us-west-2; symptoms match 502s followed by retries that led to duplicate authorizations in some flows.
- Immediate mitigation applied at 09:28: reverted the cache invalidation change and applied a temporary rate-limit on tokenization retries for requests with identical payment_nonce values.
- We're preparing an incident bundle for you (attachment: incident_log_20280329.tar.gz) and an initial RC note (initial_root_cause.txt).

Actionable next steps for AtlasPay:
1) Temporarily disable client-side automatic retry for tokenization failures (stop after one retry) — this prevents duplicate authorizations while we finalize the fix.
2) If you see any pending duplicate transactions, share the transaction IDs and we will mark them in our audit logs for reconciliation.

We will provide a postmortem and a proposed SLA credit calculation by EOD today. Marissa (CS lead) and Vivek (Ops) are looped in; Marissa will coordinate the QBR credit/contract conversation and Vivek will sign off on the technical closure.

Call to action: Can we do a 20-minute sync at 10:15 PDT to walk through the temporary mitigation and the reconciliation plan?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: incident_log_20280329.tar.gz, initial_root_cause.txt

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Mar 2028 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: AtlasPay postmortem summary + owner cadence (for QBR packet)

Confidential — internal summary and action tracker for QBR prep. (This email will form the exec summary slide for the customer-facing QBR deck.)

Executive summary (one-liner): transient cache invalidation regression during a kernel/driver update in us-west-2 caused tokenization 502s and subsequent duplicate authorizations; immediate rollback and retry throttling mitigated customer impact; full remediation plan and SLA credit calc committed.

Key timeline
- 07:45 PDT: First customer report
- 07:49 PDT: Automated alerts spike (tokenization p50->p99)
- 07:55 PDT: Identified correlated rolling kernel update as likely trigger
- 09:28 PDT: Reverted change and applied retry throttling
- 10:10 PDT: Temporary mitigation validated by AtlasPay

Why this matters to OKRs/QBR:
- This incident touches OKR INF-OKR2: reduce P99 tokenization latency and error rate by 25% this quarter. If not addressed in the long term, this pattern will block that objective and create repeated SLA spend.

Proposed owners & deliverables (short names, RACI-light):
- Short-term: retry-throttling harden + guardrails (owner: rishi_malhotra) — due 2028-04-06
- Medium-term: kernel-update compatibility test in CI (owner: infra-test-team; internal owner: rishi_malhotra) — due 2028-04-20
- Long-term: tokenization path refactor to decouple retry logic from cache invalidation (owner: inference-runtime-team; sponsor: vivek_kulkarni) — due 2028-05-15

Action items (tracked in sheet):
- A1: Confirm duplicate transaction list with AtlasPay (owner: marissa_cole) — due 2028-03-30
- A2: SLA credit calc & legal outreach draft (owner: ben_carter) — due 2028-03-29 EOD
- A3: Patch release candidate and staged rollout (owner: rishi_malhotra) — due 2028-04-04

Artifacts and links:
- Incident ticket: INF-9412
- QBR slide deck folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-atlaspay-incident
- Action tracker: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/atlaspay-incident-actions

Please reply with any corrections to owners or realistic due dates. I will convert this into the single-slide exec readout and drop a 1-paragraph customer-facing postmortem for Marissa to validate.

—Ben

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Mar 2028 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: AtlasPay postmortem summary + owner cadence (for QBR packet)

Thanks Ben — clear and actionable. A few adjustments and commitments from my side:

- A1: I'll have the duplicate transaction list by 09:30 PDT tomorrow (2028-03-30).
- A2: Ben — please send the SLA credit calc by EOD (I will route to Legal/Finance once received).
- A3 / Patch: Rishi, confirm you have CI lanes for kernel compatibility by 2028-04-06 (we can relax the medium-term deadline if you need an extra week).

AVAILABILITY: I'll prep the one-slide exec summary and a customer-facing 3-para postmortem for review by 2028-03-30 noon. Vivek — if you're OK with the proposed sponsor/owner split, I'll schedule the QBR slot for the remediation review (15 minutes) in next week's cadence.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
